description:
MEASURED 2026-08-07 (this was previously an unverified grep-level claim; it has now been benchmarked). Release build, AMD Ryzen 5 5600, rustc 1.97.0, std::time::Instant, 200-step windows per checkpoint, two 5,000-step warm-ups discarded. The temporary benchmark was deleted afterwards and the tree left byte-identical.

MECHANISM (confirmed):
crates/chem-eng-real-time-process-control-simulator/src/lib/beta_testing/stable_transfer_functions/first_order_transfer_fn.rs -- and a byte-identical twin under alpha_nightly/, which is the tier TUAS actually imports:
  :16      pub(crate) response_vec: Vec<FirstOrderResponse>,
  :113     self.response_vec.push(new_response);   -- one entry per input change; a real PID error signal changes every step (the guard at :89-92 only compares to 9 dp)
  :134-138 re-sums the ENTIRE vector every step via .iter_mut().map(|r| r.calculate_response(current_time)).sum()
  :147-230 clear_first_order_response_vector prunes via repeated .position() + .remove(index), itself O(n) per removal.

CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM -- growth is NOT unbounded in general. FirstOrderResponse::is_steady_state (:291-301) retires an entry once time_elapsed/process_time > 20.0, so the vector saturates at N = 20*tau/dt entries. Cost is linear in step index up to that horizon, then FLAT. It is unbounded only when the run never reaches 20*tau -- which is exactly what happened to teh-o-prke (tau1 ~ 80.8 s at 1 ms -> 1.6 M entries).

MEASURED per-step cost:
  A: TUAS's shipped PID, dt=0.04 s -- 5.33 us @100 -> 27.90 @1k -> 28.61 @10k -> 28.07 @39k   (total 1.13 s / 40k steps)
  B: PID, dt=0.1 s               -- 5.36 -> 11.34 -> 11.45 -> 11.46                            (0.46 s / 40k)
  C: PID, dt=0.001 s             -- 52.4 us @1k -> 259.3 @5k -> 528.3 @10k -> 1084.6 @20k -> 1131.3 @40k -> 1133.3 @79k  (79.5 s / 80k)
  D: bare ProportionalController -- 1.83 @100 -> 9.30 @1k -> 9.34 @39k                          (0.37 s / 40k)
  E: PID tau=1000 s, dt=0.04 s   -- 5.34 @100 -> 35.96 @1k -> 105.57 @5k -> 367.04 @20k -> 692.35 @39k, never plateaus (15.7 s / 40k)

O() CONCLUSION: per-step cost is O(min(n, 20*tau/dt)) -- linear in step index during the ramp, then a flat plateau. Case C is decisive: growth is exactly linear (5k->10k = 2.04x, 10k->20k = 2.05x against 2.00x step ratios) then goes flat at step 20,000 = exactly 20 s / 0.001 s, the retirement horizon. Case E, whose horizon (500,000 steps) is never reached, grows linearly for the whole run and never plateaus. So: O(n^2) total while ramping, O(n * 20*tau/dt) once saturated.
Cost per response term is constant at 9.3 / 9.5 / 9.3 / 9.4 ns/term for A/B/D/C -- which nails the mechanism quantitatively.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS EVEN THOUGH IT SATURATES: TUAS's SHIPPED config sits at a permanent flat 28 us/step for ONE PID, and it runs two PIDs plus a P block -- ~66 us/step of pure controller overhead, forever, for arithmetic that needs ~1 ns. Halving the timestep doubles it.

TWO AGGRAVATING FINDINGS:
- first_order_transfer_fn_with_zeroes.rs:27,29 carries TWO such vectors, so every first-order-with-zero block costs 2N terms.
- proportional_controller/mod.rs:29-44 implements a PURE GAIN G(s) = K_c as (K_c*s + K_c)/(s + 1) through the same machinery, so a P controller does O(20/dt) work per step. Its own doc at :58 says "probably overdoing it in terms of computation cost but that's not an issue ... yet".

TUAS PID PATH CONFIRMED (library code, not #[cfg(test)]):
crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/pre_built_components/ciet_three_branch_plus_dracs/ciet_educational_simulator_loop_prototypes/version_3/mod.rs:508-512 AnalogController::new_filtered_pid_controller(1.75, 1.75 s, 1.0 s, 1.0); second CTAH controller :521-525; ProportionalController delay block :533-536; timestep 0.04 s (:108). Also version_2.rs:482,495 and ~20 further sites in DRACS regression/validation tests, plus coupled_dracs_loop_tests/isolated_dracs_loop_resistance_calibration/mod.rs:331.

REMEDY -- copy what teh-o-prke already did. Commit 46194ba6 (2026-07-15, bead op-e46.4), single file, +229/-80: deleted the five TransferFnFirstOrder lags and replaced them with a fixed-size 5-element state array advanced by a closed-form backward-Euler recurrence (delayed_neutron_layer.rs:405-413):
    C_i^{n+1} = (C_i^n + dt*(beta_i/Lambda)*P) / (1 + dt*lambda_i)
No Vec, no history, public API unchanged, guarded by an O(1) regression test precursor_update_is_o1_per_step (:555). The precedent numbers are recorded in-tree and were verified: delayed_neutron_layer.rs:88-89 "measured ~49 us -> ~1.8 ms/step from step 1k to 40k"; :549 "Representative: ~0.7-1.0 ns/step, flat across blocks".

A first-order lag must carry ONE state variable, not a history of every input it has ever seen.

RELATED: op-e46.5 already tracks a latent second instance -- nordheim_fuchs::advance_with_reactivity_driver still takes a &mut TransferFnFirstOrder.

HARDWARE CAVEAT: absolute microsecond figures are specific to this CPU. Machine-independent are (a) the linear relation between per-step cost and step index in the ramp regime, (b) saturation landing exactly at 20*tau/dt steps, (c) cost scaling exactly with live-term count.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-11 (awaiting maintainer review; NOT closed by the agent).

APPROACH CHOSEN: option 1, the exact O(1) recurrence. Not time-bucketing. The recurrence reproduces the pre-existing semantics EXACTLY rather than approximating them, so bucketing was not implemented and no grouping error had to be quantified. It is the zero-order-hold / step-invariant discrete equivalent, exact for piecewise-constant input; module docs cite Astrom & Wittenmark, Seborg et al., Franklin/Powell/Workman, Ogata, Hochbruck & Ostermann, Oppenheim & Schafer, and Smith (open access). No editions/years/pages given -- none verified against a physical copy.

SCOPE: all FIVE vector-carrying block types, in BOTH tiers (alpha_nightly and beta_testing), not just the first-order one named in the original report:
  first_order_transfer_fn.rs                (1 vec -> 2 scalars)
  first_order_transfer_fn_with_zeroes.rs    (2 vecs -> 1 scalar)
  second_order_transfer_fn.rs               (1 vec -> 3 scalars, enum per damping regime)
  decaying_sinusoid.rs                      (1 vec -> 2 scalars, decaying rotation)
  decaying_exponentials.rs                  (1 vec -> 3 scalars; alpha_nightly only)
The two tiers are now byte-identical apart from the tier import path; previously they had drifted (beta_testing's decaying_sinusoid had a '>' vs '>=' heaviside that dropped the cosine value at t == start_time; unified on alpha's correct '>=').

MEASURED, same harness before and after (release, AMD Ryzen 5 5600, rustc 1.97.0, 200-step windows, two 5,000-step warm-ups discarded). Baseline reproduces this bead's original figures:
  A PID dt=0.04, 40k:   28.35 us/step plateau -> 0.17 us/step;  1.188 s -> 0.007 s
  B PID dt=0.10, 40k:   13.15 us/step         -> 0.17 us/step;  0.478 s -> 0.007 s
  C PID dt=0.001, 80k: 1176.11 us/step plateau -> 0.17 us/step; 83.280 s -> 0.015 s   (the decisive case)
  D P only dt=0.04:      9.42 us/step         -> 0.06 us/step;  0.379 s -> 0.002 s
  E PID tau_d=1000 dt=0.04: 736.86 us/step still rising -> 0.17 us/step; 15.167 s -> 0.007 s
  F PID tau_d=80.8 dt=0.001 (the PRKE shape): 2329.52 us/step still rising -> 0.17 us/step; 127.599 s -> 0.014 s
Per-step cost is now FLAT in the step index in every case, including E and F whose retirement horizons are never reached.

PHYSICS UNCHANGED: the summed output over each of the six runs is identical before and after to the three decimal places printed (e.g. case A sink 17175484.304 both times). The only intended difference is that the old code discarded exp(-20) = 2.06e-9 of each step response when it retired one; the recurrence carries that residual, so the new answer is marginally MORE accurate.

VERIFICATION (methodology + results in each test doc comment): each recurrence checked against the closed-form analytic superposition of the retained response structs, over 2000 steps, tolerance 1e-9. Max abs differences measured 2026-08-11: first order 6.33e-15; with zeroes 1.69e-15; second order 9.05e-15 / 5.11e-15 / 6.94e-15 (zeta = 0.35 / 1.0 / 2.4); decaying sinusoid 4.16e-16 sine, 4.86e-16 cosine; decaying exponential 8.60e-16 overdamped, 6.66e-16 critically damped; irregular time grid 7.99e-15; dead time 6.11e-15. All round-off, not discretisation error.

REGRESSION TESTS (would have caught the original defect):
  block_state_size_does_not_grow_with_step_index -- 100k steps at dt=0.001 with tau=80.8 s; state size identical at step 100 and step 99,999 ([2,1,3,2,3] alpha, [2,1,3,2] beta). Pre-0.2.0 the counts would have been 101 and 100,000.
  pid_step_cost_does_not_grow_with_step_index (alpha) -- filtered PID tau_d=80.8 s at dt=0.001: 0.172 us/step @5k -> 0.175 us/step @100k, ratio 1.02; bare P 0.059 -> 0.060, ratio 1.02.
  first_order_step_cost_does_not_grow_with_step_index (beta) -- 0.0550 -> 0.0570 us/step, ratio 1.04.

CAPABILITIES PRESERVED: irregular/arbitrary timesteps (the recurrence uses the actual elapsed time per call, verified by a dedicated test) and dead time (queued in a VecDeque bounded by delay/dt -- 26 entries for 0.25 s of dead time at dt=0.01, flat over a 2000-step run; empty when there is no dead time). New precondition, documented: simulation time must be non-decreasing.

TESTS: chem-eng 21 passed / 0 failed (--release). cargo check --workspace --lib --tests clean.

VERSION: 0.1.1 -> 0.2.0 (maintainer-authorised minor bump), plus the matching pin in the root workspace Cargo.toml. Crate stays Apache-2.0.

TEMPORARY BENCHMARK HARNESS DELETED after measuring, as before.

NOT COMMITTED -- work left in the tree for maintainer review.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
FOLLOW-UP 2026-08-11, after the work was committed in a9f71f01 by a concurrent agent (NOT by me -- I was instructed to leave it uncommitted).

FLAKY TEST FOUND AND FIXED (uncommitted, in tree). The two wall-clock step-cost regression tests I added asserted a late-vs-early ratio below 5x from a SINGLE timed 2,000-step window per checkpoint. That flaked once (31 passed / 1 failed) while other agents saturated all six cores with TUAS and tampines-steam-tables runs. A --lib rerun immediately passed 32/32, so it was scheduler noise, not a regression -- but a load-sensitive test is a bad test.

FIX: each checkpoint is now the MINIMUM of 5 repeated windows instead of one sample. Contention can only ADD wall-clock time, never remove it, so the minimum is a far more stable estimator. The 5x pass criterion was NOT loosened.

VERIFIED AFTER THE FIX, deliberately while the machine was still under heavy concurrent load:
  full crate suite run 4x: 32 passed / 0 failed every time
  alpha PID  0.279 us/step @5k -> 0.279 @100k, ratio 1.00
  alpha bare P 0.105 -> 0.104, ratio 1.00
  beta filtered derivative 0.0905 -> 0.0935, ratio 1.03
  beta pure gain 0.0913 -> 0.0943, ratio 1.03
Absolute figures are above the 0.17 us/step measured on an idle machine because of the load; the ratio is unaffected, and the ratio is what the test asserts. Doc comments updated to record both the new methodology and these numbers.

cargo check --workspace --lib --tests still exit 0.

STILL OUTSTANDING: op-wxzp (TUAS full release suite never completed) and op-i2zc (reconcile z_domain::c2d with these recurrences).

title: chem-eng: rewrite transfer functions as O(1) recurrences — MEASURED 28 us/step plateau in TUAS

description:
Four crate-level status banners in raffles say the crate is empty. It is not.

FALSE claims:
- crates/raffles/README.md:11-15  "SCAFFOLD ONLY -- nothing is implemented. This crate currently contains module boundaries, licensing and provenance, and nothing else. No distribution, no sampler, no sensitivity estimator, no surrogate."
- crates/raffles/src/lib.rs:13-18  "## Status -- SCAFFOLD ONLY / Nothing is implemented. Every module below is an empty, documented placeholder... No distribution, sampler, estimator or surrogate exists yet"
- crates/raffles/CLAUDE.md:13  "Current state: scaffold. Module boundaries, licensing and provenance only."
- workspace CLAUDE.md:830 (Members table)  "Scaffold only, nothing implemented, no human V&V."

ACTUAL state (measured 2026-08-07):
  distributions.rs  2795 lines / 1689 non-comment / 14 #[test]
  samplers.rs       1460 lines /  585 non-comment / 13 #[test]
  sensitivity.rs    1241 lines /  542 non-comment /  7 #[test]
Zero todo!()/unimplemented!() in the crate. Real public API e.g. sensitivity.rs:301 pearson_correlation, :360 spearman_correlation, :466 SobolSampleLayout; samplers.rs:772 enum Sampler, :807 fn generate. (Tests not run in this pass -- counts are #[test] attribute counts.)

WHAT IS accurate and must NOT be "fixed": surrogate.rs is genuinely empty -- 54 lines, 0 non-comment lines, and its own header (:3) plus README.md:37 correctly say so. Only the four crate-level banners are wrong.

Docs that under-report capability cause work to be redone. Correct all four; keep the "no human V&V" caveat, which is still true.
title: raffles: four crate-level docs falsely claim 'scaffold only, nothing implemented'

description: FLAGGED AS A MAINTAINER DECISION FIRST. docs/real-time-multifidelity-scoping.md recommends MSRE as the first real-time multi-fidelity demo; docs/reactor-scoping/README.md:120-133 recommends finishing the FHR widget migration first. Reconcile before starting. THE WORK, if chosen: core dwell + loop transit + recirculation-return source. Standard point kinetics is INVALID for circulating fuel, so this is genuinely new physics, not a speed hack. Derive beta_eff and the circulation reactivity loss from moltres' 300-cell spatial solve offline (measured 1.14 s/solve -- 11x too slow for a 0.1 s TH step, 1140x for a 1 ms kinetics step), then verify the reduced model against it. Both sides already exist and pass tests, so the verification target is free. A quantitative external check is waiting: the CNRS benchmark's precursor-drift worth, ~60 pcm, extracted in docs/vtb-findings.md:176-195. Also wires moltres in as an offline reference -- it currently has ZERO dependents. SCOPE HONESTLY: the deliverable is a real-time circulating-fuel PRKE twin VERIFIED AGAINST A SPATIAL SOLVER, not a validated MSRE model.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: On-device Termux testing surfaced a real gating bug --lib checks missed: examples/godiva_gpu_benchmark.rs used desktop GPU-only API (GpuContext::info, UnionTotalXs::lookup_gpu) with no Android gate, so 'cargo build'/'cargo test' in Termux (which compile examples) failed with 'no field info on GpuContext' (on Android GpuContext is the empty CPU-only stub). Fixed on develop (commit 4bb949a) by matching the njoy gpu_wmp_bench pattern: Android stub main + #[cfg(not(target_os="android"))] on every desktop item; desktop build unchanged. Swept --all-targets for the Android target across outram-blender/njoy/foam-turbulence/foam-appbuilder/tampines/nee_soon + outram-mc-libs: all clean now (godiva was the only offender). NOTE: the earlier host-side --lib sweep did NOT catch this — it only checks the library, not examples/tests/benches; --all-targets (or a native Termux cargo build) is required. Remaining: full on-device Termux build pass for all non-GUI crates.
